nodes.name: Every 15 minutes
nodes.notes: Matches the Instagram runner, so a video due at 5pm goes to both within the same quarter hour. The portal decides what is due; this only asks.

nodes.name: What is due
nodes.notes:
Replace PASTE_CRON_SECRET_HERE with the CRON_SECRET from deploy/.env — the same value the other portal workflows use.

Read-only. Five at a time, because each one downloads and re-uploads a whole video file and a run that tries twenty will still be going when the next trigger fires.

nodes.name: One video at a time
nodes.notes: An empty queue produces no items and the run simply ends here, which is the normal outcome most of the day.

nodes.name: Claim it
nodes.notes:
The lock. A conditional UPDATE in the portal decides who gets the row, so two overlapping runs can never both upload the same video.

409 here is normal, not a failure: another run got there first. neverError keeps the run alive so the IF below can skip this one and carry on.

nodes.name: Did we get it?
nodes.notes: False means somebody else has it, it is already up, or it ran out of attempts. All three mean: skip quietly.

nodes.name: Download the video
nodes.notes:
The reason this workflow exists rather than the portal doing it. YouTube needs the bytes, not a URL, and a serverless function has neither the time nor the memory to carry a 200MB file.

Ten minutes, because that is a slow office connection on a long video. The signed URL from the portal is valid for twelve hours, so it will not expire underneath this.

nodes.name: Upload to YouTube
nodes.notes:
Set up the credential once: n8n → Credentials → YouTube OAuth2 API, signed in as the account that owns the channel. Scope youtube.upload.

Category 22 is People & Blogs, the sane default for agency content. A vertical video whose title carries #Shorts becomes a Short automatically — the portal adds that suffix for Reel-format tasks.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ deliverable_id: $('Claim it').item.json.body.item.deliverable_id, status: 'posted', video_id: $json.id, url: 'https://youtu.be/' + $json.id }) }}

nodes.name: Tell the portal it worked
nodes.notes: Stores the video id and watch link, and marks it posted. Replaying this for something already posted is a no-op.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ deliverable_id: $('Claim it').item.json.body.item.deliverable_id, status: 'failed', error_message: ($json.error && ($json.error.message || $json.error)) ? String($json.error.message || $json.error).slice(0, 500) : 'Upload failed', permanent: /quotaExceeded|forbidden|unauthorized|invalid_grant|not found/i.test(String($json.error && ($json.error.message || $json.error) || '')) }) }}

nodes.name: Tell the portal it failed
nodes.notes:
Both failure paths land here — a download that would not come and an upload YouTube refused.

The portal decides whether to try again; this only reports. `permanent` is a hint for the cases where another go plainly cannot help: a revoked credential, a channel that is gone, a daily quota already spent. Getting the hint wrong is safe either way — the attempt budget stops it regardless.
